curation.notes: Home-built single-trap optical tweezers active microrheology: microbeads embedded in collagen and fibrin gels are dragged at 1 μm/s to obtain local nonlinear force-displacement responses, and 4.5 μm beads are dragged near MDA-MB-231 cells (± blebbistatin) to map local matrix stiffness and the nonlinear length scale R*. Flat-punch indentation (Bruker Hysitron BioSoft), confocal PIV and simulations are separate complementary methods.

evidence.snippet: The tweezers are calibrated in phosphate-buffered saline solution. The power spectrum density method is used (47). The trap stiffness is 15 pN/μm.

bead_size.note: two bead sizes used: 2 μm and 4.5 μm (4.5 μm beads for measurements around cells)

evidence.snippet: Microparticles (2 μm, C37278, ThermoFisher, and 4.5 μm carboxylate microspheres, Polyscience) are embedded in the gel prior to polymerization.
Home-built optical tweezers are used (47). The laser beam is moved at a constant velocity of 1 μm s−1.
To make 1 mL 4 mg mL−1 collagen gels, 400 μL 10 mg mL−1 collagen solution (Advance Biomatrix, Cat# 5133) is mixed with 460 μL Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM)
To make 1 mL 3 mg mL−1 fibrin gels, 500 μL 6 mg mL−1 fibrinogen (F8630-1G, Sigma-Aldrich) solution is mixed with 500 μL 4 U mL−1 thrombin (T4648-1KU, Sigma-Aldrich).
We mixed 4.5-μm-diameter beads (Polysciences, 17140-5) with cells in the collagen solution prepared with the same protocol described above.
